edits.value_json: 四 means “four.” One account sees four counting rods representing that number. Other proposals treat 四 as an earlier graph for 泗, depicting nasal discharge, or as a graph for 呬, depicting breath, later borrowed for “four.” The proposed borrowings remain unestablished.

The formation is disputed. One interpretation reads the graph as four counting rods representing four. A distinct proposal treats 四 as the original graph of 泗, depicting nasal discharge, later borrowed to write “four”; its proponent noted that this proposal lacks textual attestation. Another account identifies 四 with a graph for 呬 depicting breath, then proposes borrowing it for “four” because the words may have sounded similar. Neither proposed borrowing is established, and the referent’s original name is unknown.

One interpretation proposes that 四 began as a graph depicting breath, identified with 呬, and was reused to write “four” because the words may have sounded similar. In one reported Old Chinese reconstruction system, 呬 is *hrids and 四 is *hljids. A separate proposal treats 四 as the original graph of 泗, depicting nasal discharge, and says 四 was then borrowed for “four”; this proposal lacks textual attestation. Neither account establishes the depicted referent’s original spoken name or proves that borrowing occurred.
